title: Enfusion mod
description: The one file a mod is configured by, the way package.json configures a package. What belongs to the machine — where DayZ is, which key signs the pbo — lives in the VS Code settings instead, so that a file under git never carries it.

$schema.description: The schema this file is written against, for an editor that finds it that way rather than by the file name.

name.description: The mod's name, which is one name and not a title: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore, excluding Windows device names such as CON and LPT1. The panel shows it, the prefix root goes onto the work drive under it (P:\<name>), and the build writes it into @<name>. The name of the mod's own folder when left out, so a folder called something else than the mod — client, holding CADNavigationClient — is exactly what this is written for. It is the same name as dir in the CfgMods of the main addon; the two disagreeing means the game loads one mod and the extension builds another.

description.description: What the mod does, in a sentence.

exclude.description: File masks and folder names the builder is not to pack: model sources, texture sources, anything a pbo has no business carrying. Left out, a default list of the source formats DayZ modding has settled on is used; naming any replaces that list whole. Handed to pboProject as it is written here. AddonBuilder ignores it: the option it takes an exclude list through crashes it.

launch.description: How this mod is launched. Ignored whole where the workspace has a workspace.enf: that file owns launch.
Everything about getting the game up: where the built mods are, which third-party mods join them, and what the Run and Debug list offers.

modsDirectory.description: Where the @<Mod> folders live: the builder writes them here, and the game is pointed at them here. A relative path is counted from the folder this file is in, which is what keeps it meaning the same thing on every machine that clones the repository.

mods.description: Mods loaded by both the client and server as -mod=, in load order, by folder name in modsDirectory, with or without the leading @. Workspace mods must also be named here to load.

serverMods.description: Additional mods loaded only by the server as -serverMod=, in load order, named the same way as mods. Shared mods belong in mods and do not need to be repeated here.

targets.description: The entries of the Run and Debug list. Each one says what to put up and where its profile and mission come from.

name.description: What the Run and Debug list shows this target as.

mod.description: The mod the profile, the mission and the server.cfg come from. The mod being launched when left out.

map.description: The world this target is about, which is the tail of the mission folder name — sakhal, chernarusplus. A server loads the mission the target's mod keeps for it, Missions\<Mod>.<map>, with the Global and Dev layers of Missions laid over it; a client with no server to join loads dayzOffline.<map> instead.

enumDescriptions: The server, and a client that joins it.

experimental.description: Start this target from the separately installed DayZ Experimental client and server applications instead of the stable ones.

mods.description: Shared mods loaded by both the client and server for this target. Left out, the launch block's mods are inherited; when present, this list replaces them whole, including when it is empty.

serverMods.description: Additional mods loaded only by the server for this target. Left out, the launch block's serverMods are inherited; when present, this list replaces them whole, including when it is empty.

serverConfig.description: The server.cfg the dev server is started with, relative to the target's mod. Left out, the mod's own server.cfg is used, and failing that the one beside the file that owns this launch block.
